title: Seaetto's Cipher
text: This was a little while after Assistant, Rival's true body, and her parent had joined the group, I say. For some reason, Rafumi was holding the hammer Seven Star Weapon.
“Vof!?”
At the sight, Wolf and the Siltvelt envoy froze speechless, pointing at it.
“Hey, Rafumi! What in the world is that, I say!?”
Of all things, Rafumi was holding something that looked exactly like the hammer Seven Star Weapon, so I simply couldn't help but point it out.
“Ah, this? Why hide it—this is the Vassal Weapon of what's called the Seven Star Weapons, the sacred hammer. What of it?”
“Why are you acting so puzzled!? That's the very thing we stripped from Takt and enshrined in Faubrey, I say!”

Rafumi declared it as if it were the most natural thing in the world. Wolf, too, had personally witnessed the hammer being stripped from Takt when they'd handed him over to the Faubrey king, so he stood frozen in shock. Generally speaking, the Seven Star Weapons chose their next wielder by embedding themselves in a rock at a nearby altar. During the loop when we'd gone to Faubrey, reincarnators had apparently been regularly challenging the ritual to become the hammer's wielder, only to be judged and rejected. So what was the deal with Rafumi just casually bringing it along like it was nothing, I say?
“That's why I went and fetched it myself, making it look as though I'd acquired it through the proper method, and brought it here.”
“So you're saying it just looks like you acquired it properly?”
“That makes you just like the reincarnators! Disposal time, I say!”
“Hmph… don't lump me in with the likes of them. Then take this—Thor Hammer VI!”
Rafumi dodged my attack, spun around once, and slammed the hammer down on me!
“Fube!?”
I got crushed by the crackling, electrified hammer. Since I'd properly boosted my stats, I was able to get right back up, but it was a solid, heavily-enhanced blow, I say.
“Vaf… you're actually handling the weapon well?”
“I'm originally an event spirit myself, you know. Conversing with spirits is easy enough for me. Rather than let it fall into the hands of those reincarnators, I got its consent and I'm using it.”
“Seems like it'll cause quite a stir once an actual wielder shows up, though.”

“I've already smoothed things over. I told them I'm a collaborator with the Shield and Spear Hero's party, and that I took custody of it rather than let it fall to the likes of Takt. Well, unlike the reincarnators who—as the Spear Hero can attest—couldn't draw out the weapon's power, I demonstrated I could, and it agreed without a second thought.”
Grr… Rafumi! There ought to be limits to doing whatever she pleases, I say.
“Word's already quietly gotten through to Siltvelt. I imagine we'll hear back from them soon.”
“What in the world are you planning, I say!?”
“It's nothing so grand—more fighting power never hurts, does it? Well, once the hammer finds a wielder it likes, it'll leave my hands and settle with them.”
“Given what happened with Takt, I'd rather you not go around doing whatever you please…”
There's a limit to how free-spirited one can be, I say.
“No harm done, surely? Speaking of which—Wolf, was it? Haven't you yourself failed to fully draw out the power of the Claw?”
“V-Vof…”
Wolf let out the sound with a face like he'd bitten into a bitter bug.
“Well, that seems to be a matter of your own heart, but if I may offer some friendly advice—the Claw isn't rejecting you at all. It's you who can't use it.”
Rafumi seemed to be lecturing Wolf about something. If he couldn't draw out the Claw's power, it should just go settle in Filo-tan's hands instead, I say.
“Um… so you're saying you're using the hammer Seven Star Weapon as a temporary wielder?”
“That's right. Well, once this one finds a wielder it likes, we just need to report it to the country at that point—simple as that.”
“It'd be a problem if the wielder kept changing so easily though… the higher-ups are already confused enough because of Takt's case.”
“Hmm… I'll handle it properly next loop, then. By the way, apparently the hammer currently has its eye on a potential wielder right here.”
“There's someone here who could become its rightful wielder?”

If so, I wished it would hurry up and leave Rafumi's hands already, I say. To begin with, the hammer was also one of Big Sister's weapons, so personally, I wasn't too fond of them. Back in the first world, whenever I peeked, I was often threatened with one, after all.
“It seems interested in Larsazusa's grandfather. From aptitude to everything else, he's currently recognized as immediate combat strength.”

Panda's grandfather, huh. He certainly is quite the formidable fighter. He seemed to use a kiseru pipe as his weapon. Come to think of it, Panda's weapon changes between Claw and hammer whenever she's chosen as a hero. It seemed Panda's grandfather had the qualifications too, I say.
“Well, this one chose an otherworlder during the summoning ritual, only to have Takt snatch it away right after. Just bad timing, really. Bad luck too, that there wasn't a candidate nearby.”
I figured suddenly trying to hand the hammer to Panda's grandfather and make him the Hammer Hero would raise suspicion too, I say.
“In any case, having it around lets me do all sorts of things, so I'll keep using it.”
“Wouldn't it look suspicious if someone disguised as the Sword Hero suddenly started using a hammer?”
“That's no problem either. Disguising my appearance is trivial, and besides, I can split myself in the first place.”
“…At this point, shouldn't you just save the world yourself?”
“Hmph… I'm not so tasteless as to go that far. Besides, I already told you I can't fully draw out its performance.”
Is there anything this Rafumi *can't* do at this point, I say? And that's the story of how Rafumi ended up bringing out the hammer Seven Star Weapon before anyone even noticed.

A few days after Rafumi had secretly taken possession of the hammer Seven Star Weapon, I say. Since I'd been asked to spar with them, I joined in on Éclair and the others' training session. Granny was absorbed in training together with Panda's grandfather, drilling Panda, Elephant, and Older Sister. That day, after training, Éclair seemed to be sorting through her personal belongings. Crocodile Guy was with her too. It looked like the sort of tidying-up you do after working up a good sweat.
“Come to think of it…”

As if remembering something, Éclair glanced at Crocodile Guy before picking up a portrait of her father. What was going on, I wondered? It had been damaged before, but it looked like it had already been repaired.
“Eclair-sama, what are you doing?”
“Shion, you… did you hear anything from Father? I just remembered him telling me that if something ever happened to him, if the people were ever in danger… I should check the portrait.”
But when she turned the unfolded portrait over, there didn't seem to be anything special on the back. Maybe it was some kind of invisible ink or something, I wondered?
“At first I thought there might be a letter hidden in the frame or the painting itself, but since it got torn, I figured it was gone by now—though I thought there might be some other possibility.”
“Hm? Now that you mention it… I was taught that if Eclair-sama ever asked me about a secret, I should tell her to turn it upside down.”
“Upside down?”
Éclair turned the portrait upside down.
“Is there anything different…?”
“I'm not really sure either… Was there anyone else he left a message with? Like my own father, maybe?”
“Do you really think Father would ask for something that complicated?”
“I can't say it's impossible.”

This was… that! A mystery that these two simply didn't have the brainpower to solve, I say! It was the kind of puzzle that needed someone with far greater wit to figure out. Someone like Father, for instance. No—Motoyasu here shall solve it himself, I say! My brain, the very one that put on a deduction show for Takt and the others and turned it into an unsolved case, was about to shine.
“Well then, let this clever fellow have a look, I say.”
“No, I'm quite certain you won't figure it out.”
“Can Kitamura-dono really solve this given the flow of things? If anything, it'd probably be faster to ask Iwatani-dono, Amaki-dono, Theodore, or—though I wouldn't rely on her too much—Rafumi-dono…”
Ignoring the skeptical Crocodile Guy and Éclair, I examined the upside-down portrait. Hmph!
“It's a face even upside down, I say!”
It had to be some kind of trick picture, I say.
“…Just as expected of that head of yours.”
“What's that supposed to mean!? Are you calling me stupid!?”
As I fumed indignantly, Crocodile Guy and Éclair both looked away.
“Right, right. If I had to point something out, it'd be how the pattern on this frame looks like text when flipped upside down, I say.”
